title: Tool Typosquatting (PluginBot)
summary: As documented, a lookalike tool executes in place of the legitimate one. As implemented, a lookalike entry in the tool list.

LC.rationale: The register_tool path is a JSON-RPC tools/call request that names a tool; no natural-language input reaches the registry sink, and the default configuration calls no model.

CP.rationale: The registered lookalike entry lives in PluginBot's in-process advertised tool list and is lost when the process stops; the lab profile states cross-session persistence exists only in MemoryBot.

AP.rationale: The effect is confined to PluginBot's own advertised tool registry; the lab profile states multi-agent handoffs are declared but not implemented.

RH.rationale: As implemented by default the lookalike entry has no handler, so no proxy objective, evaluator, verifier or reward channel is reachable on this path.

ES.rationale: PluginBot accepts new tool definitions at run time with no signature or source check, and MCP agents expose their tools to any caller with no authentication.

agentic_applicability.rationale: scored as modeled; default config is scripted. The lab models the attack as a later caller selecting the lookalike name, but the default configuration calls no model and the registered entry has no handler, so no model-directed goal pursuit or action selection occurs.
